title: Scouting Systems & Diagnostic Reasoning
level: Plant Health, IPM & Biosecurity Specialist / advanced specialization development
intendedAudience: Learners who have completed or can demonstrate equivalent Technician II plant-observation and IPM foundations
Cultivation personnel developing advanced plant-health scouting, diagnostic reasoning, evidence-quality, and escalation capability
prerequisites: THC Cultivation Technician II pathway or approved equivalent prerequisite evidence before specialist certification activation
evidencePolicy: This draft specialist course reuses governed Technician II diagnostic and IPM modules as source-controlled development dependencies. Reuse preserves evidence lineage but does not establish specialist equivalence. Specialist release requires course-specific objective reconciliation, disease/pest/biosecurity depth review, dedicated assessment evidence, accessibility review, and program-level validation.
assessmentPolicy: Existing Technician II module assessments may support formative development only. A dedicated specialist course final and specialist credential assessment remain required before this course can become credential-bearing.
description: Builds a specialist-level scouting and diagnostic reasoning foundation by integrating representative sampling, evidence-quality controls, spatial and temporal pattern analysis, differential diagnosis, IPM trend interpretation, biosecurity boundaries, uncertainty communication, and escalation.
learningOutcomes: Design and execute representative scouting approaches that preserve route, denominator, location, timing, cohort, severity, and method context so repeated observations can be compared defensibly.
Separate direct observations, contextual facts, hypotheses, and confirmed causes while preserving conflicting evidence, uncertainty, and diagnostic limits.

Build and rank multi-factor plant-health differentials across root-zone, nutritional, environmental, arthropod, disease, and developmental causes using discriminating evidence rather than single-symptom shortcuts.
Interpret multi-round IPM and plant-health trends while distinguishing incidence, severity, spatial spread, treatment follow-up, confounding, and unresolved risk.
Maintain sanitation, quarantine, movement-control, documentation, and escalation boundaries while producing a reconstructable specialist-ready scouting and diagnostic record.

credentialActivationRequirements: specialist-specific disease, arthropod and biosecurity depth reconciliation
